I have resolved the issue where deferred fields were incorrect when following prefetches back to a parent object.

### Cause of the Issue
When evaluating prefetches for `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor`, `get_prefetch_queryset()` sets the parent object on the relation cache for each prefetched related object.

However, when evaluating the inner prefetch queryset, any nested prefetches configured on that queryset (e.g. `Prefetch('user', queryset=User.objects.only('kind'))`) are executed during iteration of that queryset. These inner prefetches correctly populate the relation cache on the related objects with the custom query results.

Previously, `get_prefetch_queryset()` unconditionally set/overwrote the cached relation on the related object with the outer parent instance (which had its own, potentially different set of deferred fields). This caused the inner custom-prefetched instance to be replaced by the outer instance with different deferred fields, triggering extra queries when accessing fields that were loaded by the inner prefetch.

### Solution
In [`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1mbfl1oa/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L145-L150), `get_prefetch_queryset()` now checks whether the relation on the related object is already cached before populating the reverse relation cache. If a relation cache already exists (from a nested prefetch executed on the inner queryset), it is preserved rather than overwritten.
